q0.t: Question 1. We, blank, to the beach last summer.

q0_a0.t: We went to the beach last summer.

q0_a1.t: We have gone to the beach last summer.

q0_a2.t: We go to the beach last summer.

q0_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: went. Last summer is a finished time, so we use the simple past. Go is irregular: went.

q0_ok.t: Correct! Last summer is a finished time, so we use the simple past. Go is irregular: went.

q1.t: Question 2. They, blank, football when it started to rain.

q1_a0.t: They are playing football when it started to rain.

q1_a1.t: They were playing football when it started to rain.

q1_a2.t: They have played football when it started to rain.

q1_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: were playing. It's a long action interrupted by a short one, so we use the past continuous: were playing.

q1_ok.t: Correct! It's a long action interrupted by a short one, so we use the past continuous: were playing.

q2.t: Question 3. By the time the police arrived, the thieves, blank.

q2_a0.t: By the time the police arrived, the thieves have escaped.

q2_a2.t: By the time the police arrived, the thieves had escaped.

q2_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: had escaped. The thieves escaped before the police arrived, so we use the past perfect: had escaped.

q2_ok.t: Correct! The thieves escaped before the police arrived, so we use the past perfect: had escaped.

q3_a0.t: I knew Laura for ten years. We are still best friends.

q3_a1.t: I have known Laura for ten years. We are still best friends.

q3_a2.t: I know Laura for ten years. We are still best friends.

q3_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: have known. They are still friends now, so with for we use the present perfect: have known.

q4_a0.t: I have a shower when the phone rang.

q4_a1.t: I am having a shower when the phone rang.

q4_a2.t: I was having a shower when the phone rang.

q4_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: was having. The shower was in progress when the phone interrupted it, so we use the past continuous.

q4_ok.t: Correct! The shower was in progress when the phone interrupted it, so we use the past continuous.

q5.t: Question 6. She failed the exam because she, blank.

q5_a0.t: She failed the exam because she hadn't studied.

q5_a1.t: She failed the exam because she hasn't studied.

q5_a2.t: She failed the exam because she doesn't study.

q5_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: hadn't studied. Not studying came before failing the exam, so we use the past perfect: hadn't studied.

q5_ok.t: Correct! Not studying came before failing the exam, so we use the past perfect: hadn't studied.

s0_0_0.t: Hello, and welcome to Past Lab!

s0_1_0.t: This educational app has been made by Nuria Calvo, an English teacher at IES Goya, Zaragoza.

s0_2_0.t: [energetic] In English, we have several past tenses, and each one tells a different part of the story.

s0_2_2.t: [firm, smiling] No way! And by the end of this lesson, you'll use them all.

s0_3_0.t: Today you'll learn the simple past, the past continuous and the past perfect. And how to choose between the simple past and the present perfect!

s1_1_0.t: We use it for finished actions at a specific time in the past: yesterday, last week, two days ago.

s1_1_2.t: [energetic] Exactly! And we watched a film last night.

s1_2_0.t: Regular verbs add -ed, but irregular verbs have their own form. Go becomes went.

s1_2_2.t: [firm, correcting at once] No! Go is irregular. Yesterday I went to the park!

s1_2_3.t: S: [repeating carefully] Yesterday I went to the park.

s1_3_0.t: In negatives and questions, we use did, and the verb goes back to the infinitive.

s1_3_1.t: S: [unsure, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] She didn't went to school.

s1_3_2.t: [firm] Careful! After didn't, no past form: she didn't go to school. And in questions: did you see the match?

s1_4_0.t: With the verb be, it's was or were, and no did.

s1_4_1.t: S: [trying it out] The children were very tired. And where were you born?

s2_1_0.t: The form is: was or were, plus a verb ending in -ing.

s2_1_1.t: S: [checking] I was working, they were working?

s2_2_0.t: We use it for an action in progress at a moment in the past.

s2_2_1.t: S: [trying it out] At eight o'clock last night, I was having dinner.

s2_2_2.t: [energetic] Right! It was in progress at eight o'clock.

s2_3_0.t: We also use it to describe the background of a story.

s2_3_1.t: S: [dreamy] The sun was shining and the birds were singing.

s2_4_0.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] They was playing football.

s2_4_1.t: [firm, stopping the student] Stop! With they, use were. They were playing football.

s2_4_2.t: S: [proud] They were playing football. Easy!

s2_5_0.t: And state verbs like know, like or want never go in the continuous.

s2_5_1.t: S: [unsure, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I was knowing the answer.

s3_1_0.t: The form is: had, plus the past participle. It's the past before the past.

s3_1_1.t: S: [checking] I had seen, she had seen, they had seen?

s3_2_0.t: We use it for an action that happened before another past action.

s3_2_1.t: S: [trying it out] When we got to the cinema, the film had already started.

s3_2_2.t: [energetic] Perfect! First the film started, then you arrived.

s3_3_0.t: It's great for explaining causes, and it often goes with by the time and already.

s3_3_1.t: S: [thinking it through] By the time the police arrived, the thieves had escaped.

s3_4_0.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] When I got home, I realised I have lost my keys.

s3_4_1.t: [firm] No! You lost them before you realised. Say: I realised I had lost my keys.

s3_4_2.t: S: [repeating carefully] I realised I had lost my keys.

s3_5_0.t: S: [unsure, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] After she has finished her homework, she went out.

s3_5_1.t: [firm] Careful! It all happened in the past: after she had finished her homework, she went out.

s4_0_0.t: [energetic] Chapter four: simple past or present perfect?

s4_1_0.t: The simple past is finished, and we say when. The present perfect connects with now, and we don't say when.

s4_1_1.t: S: [confused] Hmm... So how do I choose?

s4_2_0.t: Yesterday, last year, ago and questions with when take the simple past.

s4_2_1.t: S: [trying it out] Last year my parents bought a new car. When did you buy your phone?

s4_3_0.t: Ever, never, yet, already, so far, this week, for and since take the present perfect.

s4_3_1.t: S: [curious] Have you ever met a famous person?

s4_3_2.t: [cheerful] Yes, I have! And I've lived in Zaragoza for ten years.

s4_5_0.t: And for people who are no longer alive, the simple past: Picasso painted thousands of works of art.

s5_1_0.t: S: [confused] Simple, continuous, perfect... I always mix them up!

s5_1_1.t: [energetic] Here's the trick: draw the timeline of the story.

s5_2_0.t: A long action goes in the past continuous. A short action that interrupts it goes in the simple past.

s5_2_1.t: S: [trying it out] I was having a shower when the phone rang.

s5_2_2.t: [energetic] Perfect! While goes with the long action.

s5_3_0.t: Actions one after another? All in the simple past. An action before another one? The past perfect.

s5_4_0.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I was having a shower when the phone was ringing.

s5_5_0.t: S: [unsure, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] When I got to the party, Tom went home, so I didn't see him.

s6_0_0.t: [energetic] Chapter six: the top five mistakes. Let's check them one by one!

s6_1_0.t: Mistake number one: adding -ed to irregular verbs.

s6_1_2.t: [firm] I bought a new phone! Buy is irregular.

s6_2_0.t: Mistake number two: a past form after did.

s6_2_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] Did you saw the match?

s6_2_2.t: [firm] Did you see the match? After did, the infinitive!

s6_3_0.t: Mistake number three: mixing up was and were.

s6_3_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] We was very tired.

s6_3_2.t: [firm] We were very tired! You, we and they take were.

s6_4_0.t: Mistake number four: ago with the present perfect.

s6_4_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I have lost my keys two days ago.

s6_5_0.t: And mistake number five: no participle after had.

s6_5_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I had never be on a plane.

s6_5_2.t: [firm] I had never been on a plane! Had, plus the past participle.

s6_5_3.t: S: [proud] Got it! No more mistakes!

s7_0_0.t: [energetic] Time for a challenge! Choose the right past tense for each sentence.

s8_1_0.t: Now you know the simple past, the past continuous and the past perfect, and how to choose between the simple past and the present perfect.

s8_2_0.t: This educational app was made by Nuria Calvo, an English teacher at IES Goya, Zaragoza. Now it's your turn: click the button and practise with the exercises.

s8_2_1.t: S: [cheerful, waving goodbye] See you in class!
